analysis.title: Natural Gas Comment: Europe Winter Tracker: TTF Pricing High Winter Tightness Risk
key_insights: TTF is up 8% week over week at 95 EUR/MWh. The Dec26 TTF contract, also at 95 EUR/MWh, implies a 73% market-perceived probability of a low-Mideast-LNG-supply winter, up from 51% last week.
The implied probability is calculated against GS's rising-winter-supply base case of 70 EUR/MWh and its low-winter-supply scenario of 105 EUR/MWh for Dec26 TTF.

Month-to-date Persian Gulf LNG exports have averaged 30% of normal, above GS's 20% October base case. A rise in tanker attacks near Hormuz earlier in October has kept daily tanker crossings volatile and forward supply highly uncertain.
UK Maritime Trading Operations data shows tanker attacks have dropped over the past 10 days, which suggests a potential rebound in Mideast energy exports ahead.
NW European gas balances softened marginally week over week, mainly because of warmer October weather. GS now expects regional storage to end the month 64% full, versus 63% previously.

Asia LNG demand is firming. China LNG imports for the last two weeks are up year over year, consistent with China rebuilding gas storage ahead of winter. The reported September gas storage build beat GS expectations.

GS reads the Qatari deal to buy US LNG, announced last week, as a push for long-term geographic diversification and potentially an indirect increase in Qatari market share. It sees limited insight in the deal about the duration of the Mideast conflict.

GS gives two reasons the Qatari deal says little about conflict duration: deliveries run 2030-2054, and Qatari LNG exports have already partially rebounded under a still volatile environment. Qatar also guided to first LNG from its export capacity expansion in 1Q27.
GS continues to see risks to its winter TTF forecast skewed to the upside.
US LNG loadings continue to favor Europe over Asia. The JKM-TTF spread picked up over the last week, reflecting firmer Asia LNG demand.

NW Europe industrial gas demand continues to rise, nearing 2025 levels. Low river water levels continue to weigh on NW European nuclear generation, but this was offset last week by high wind generation.

NW Europe weather forecasts turned colder than average toward the end of the 2-week window, and the November forecast flipped colder week over week despite a significantly warmer than average October.

Above GS's 20% October base case but volatile, tied to tanker attacks near Hormuz.

Assumes Persian Gulf LNG exports improve gradually to 2/3 of normal in Jan27 and a maximum of 83% in Feb27.
Assumes LNG flows stay at 25% of normal through Nov26-Mar27.

risk_factors: A prolonged low Mideast LNG supply winter would push Dec26 TTF toward GS's 105 EUR/MWh scenario.
Tanker attacks near Hormuz keep daily crossings volatile and forward supply highly uncertain.
A colder than average winter would raise prices further. GS shows 115 EUR/MWh at 1 standard deviation colder than average.
Low river water levels continue to weigh on NW European nuclear generation.
Damage to Qatari export infrastructure caps recovery in Persian Gulf LNG at a maximum of 83% of normal in Feb27 in the base case.

tension_points.bull_case: Tanker attacks near Hormuz have dropped over the past 10 days per UKMTO, and Persian Gulf LNG exports at 30% of normal run above GS's 20% October base case. Qatar has already begun a partial rebound, which points to improving supply and lower prices.
tension_points.bear_case: Dec26 TTF at 95 EUR/MWh prices a 73% chance of a low-supply winter. Forward supply is highly uncertain, and a low-supply scenario with LNG flows at 25% of normal through winter puts Dec26 TTF at 105 EUR/MWh.
tension_points.what_invalidates: LNG flows staying at 25% of normal through Nov26-Mar27 would confirm the low-supply scenario at 105 EUR/MWh, while Persian Gulf exports reaching 2/3 of normal in Jan27 would match the 70 EUR/MWh base case.
